Rule-based: CMS selected-drug lists by initial price applicability year, published maximum fair prices, Part D redesign manufacturer discount mechanics, and the Federal Register status (proposed, final, enjoined) of most-favoured-nation actions and Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff proceedings. Sources are the H1 2026 results-presentation pipeline table, ClinicalTrials.gov timing records and FDA action-date announcements. Axis one, entry timing for horizon-LOE products: earliest listed patent expiry, reference-product exclusivity expiry for biologics, and any settlement-implied or litigation-contingent date, carried as a range not a point. Axis two, US net-price realisation: (a) enacted rules and disclosed company-specific undertakings only, (b) MFN-style policy implemented, (c) tariff pass-through. Company-specific register from the 20-F risk factors and litigation note, with each entry carrying its source and its as-of date. AstraZeneca's rationale for adding a direct NYSE listing cited the US as having the world's largest and most liquid public equity markets by capitalisation and the largest pool of biopharma investors, framed as broadening access to capital and investors rather than as a trading signal.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: No peer multiple facts were supplied to me, so this rests partly on convention for large-cap diversified pharma — the operator should know that. It is anchored to the derived economics rather than picked flat: EBIT margin averages 14.2% but is rising (23.4% in FY2025), and D&A intensity (0.1147) far exceeds capex (0.0334), so EBITDA is large relative to EBIT and a mid-range multiple is the conservative read. That D&A-capex gap reflects amortised acquired intangibles that must be replenished by M&A, which a DCF's perpetuity treats as free cash. For that reason I regard this exit multiple as the better terminal anchor than the growth perpetuity, which would imply a materially higher figure. Raise toward 12x if margin expansion proves durable.

caveats: Book equity was used as the equity weight because no market capitalisation was available. Book value is what the shares were issued and retained for rather than what they are worth, and for a profitable company it is usually far lower — so the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high.

More than three quarters of the enterprise value is terminal value. The explicit forecast is contributing little, so the answer rests almost entirely on the terminal assumption rather than on the projected years a reader can check.

The two terminal methods disagree by more than a quarter. That is information, not an error: they are two different guesses about the same unknowable quantity, and the distance between them is the honest width of the answer.

The bridge from enterprise value to equity value is net debt alone. Associate holdings, minority interests and pension deficits are not read off the filings by this build, so a business carrying material non-operating items is valued as though it does not.
